study.title: Interactive dynamic scalp acupuncture enhances brain functional connectivity in bilateral basal ganglia ischemic stroke patients: a randomized controlled trial
study.randomization: Patients were randomized to IDSA (n = 35) or Sham IDSA (n = 35) therapy
study.blinding: Sham IDSA used blunt needles without skin penetration to mimic the procedure; blinding details for assessors not explicitly reported
study.population: BBGIS patients aged 45–75 years, 1–3 months post-stroke, Brunnstrom stage II–V; and age-and sex-matched healthy controls
study.inclusion_criteria: (1) a clinical diagnosis of bilateral basal ganglia and internal capsule stroke confirmed by a neurologist through comprehensive neurological examination and brain imaging (MRI or computed tomography); (2) aged between 45 and 75 years; (3) clear consciousness, absence of significant cognitive impairment, and ability to actively participate in rehabilitation training; (4) Brunnstrom stage II-V motor recovery in both proximal and distal segments of the affected limb; and (5) first-time stroke occurring within 1–3 months prior to enrollment. All participants confirmed right-handed using the Edinburgh Handedness Inventory (scores > 40). Healthy controls recruited through community advertising and had no history of neurological disorders.
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) significant medical conditions warranting exclusion were defined as: Uncontrolled hypertension (BP > 160/100 mmHg); (2) Severe cardiopulmonary disease (NYHA Class III/IV); (3) Active systemic illnesses (e.g., renal failure with GFR < 30, metastatic cancer); (4) Any condition that could substantially interfere with rehabilitation participation

arms.dropouts: 4 excluded (part of the 8 BBGIS patients excluded overall: 3 recurrent strokes, 2 venous thromboses, 3 early discharges; exact per-arm breakdown not reported)
4 excluded (part of the 8 BBGIS patients excluded overall; exact per-arm breakdown not reported)

interventions.stimulation_type: Manual scalp acupuncture combined with active limb movement
acupoints_used_exact: MS6 (anterior oblique line of the vertex-temporal)
interventions.anatomical_location_exact: Bilaterally on the scalp, targeting the anterior oblique line of the vertex-temporal (MS6) acupoint; needles inserted at the upper 1/5 and middle 2/5 positions
interventions.penetration_exact: Yes; needles inserted into sheath aponeurosis
interventions.depth_exact: Inserted until reaching the sheath aponeurosis
interventions.manipulation_exact: Needles rotated at 200 revolutions per minute to induce a tolerable sensation of soreness and swelling; alternately manipulated for 3 min each, with 5-min intervals between rotations
interventions.deqi_intended_exact: Yes; tolerable sensation of soreness and swelling (Deqi sensation)
interventions.needle_retention_exact: not_reported explicitly; needles retained during active movement period
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: During needle retention, patients were encouraged to perform active movements of the affected limb or walking exercises
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: IDSA emphasizes dynamic sensorimotor integration by requiring patients to perform targeted limb movements or walking exercises during needle manipulation; 200 rpm rotation speed selected based on previous optimization studies demonstrating this frequency optimally elicits Deqi sensation while maintaining patient comfort during dynamic movement tasks

interventions.stimulation_type: Sham scalp acupuncture with blunt needle
interventions.penetration_exact: No; blunt needle did not penetrate the skin
interventions.manipulation_exact: Manipulation techniques were identical to IDSA group
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: Patients were also encouraged to perform active movements or walking exercises during the retention period
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: Used to mimic the IDSA procedure as sham control

neuroimaging_methods.sequence_exact: Functional MRI: interleaved gradient echo-planar imaging (EPI) sequence; Structural: axial T1-weighted MPRAGE (magnetization-prepared rapid acquisition gradient echo)
neuroimaging_methods.scan_duration_exact: 8.06 min (functional, 240 EPI volumes acquired); approximately 6 min (structural)
neuroimaging_methods.preprocessing_software_exact: Data Processing Assistant for rs-fMRI (DPARSF V2.3)

neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: Data with head motion exceeding 1.5 mm in translation or 1.5° in rotation were excluded

extraction_notes.note: The paper states 70 patients were randomized (35 IDSA, 35 Sham), but the final cohort analyzed was 62 patients (31 per group). The flow diagram caption states final allocation as IDSA n=31, Sham n=31, HCs n=35, but the abstract reports IDSA n=35 and Sham n=35 as randomized. The 8 BBGIS exclusions (3 recurrent strokes, 2 venous thromboses, 3 early discharges) appear to be post-randomization dropouts, but the exact per-arm distribution of these dropouts is not reported.

The total n_analyzed_neuroimaging is ambiguous. The study enrolled 62 BBGIS patients and 35 HCs for fMRI. The baseline between-group comparison used all BBGIS patients (n=62) and HCs (n=35), total 97. The post-treatment analysis used IDSA (n=31) and Sham (n=31), total 62. These are reported separately in the relevant contrasts.

Table 1 reports BBGIS group n=70 and HC group n=40 for behavioral characteristics, which appear to be the enrolled (pre-exclusion) numbers. However the final analyzed neuroimaging cohort was 62 BBGIS + 35 HCs. This inconsistency is preserved as reported.

Table 2 lists some conditions as 'Short FCD' and others as 'Long FCD' but the text result section does not always distinguish which FCD type (short vs. long) each region represents for the key results (SMA_R described as short FCD in table, C8_R as long FCD). This distinction is preserved as in Table 2.

The FMA scores reported in the abstract (53.23 ± 13.6 vs. Sham 44.35 ± 11.2, p < 0.05) and in Figure 7 (P = 0.010) are consistent. However, the abstract states 'p < 0.05' while Figure 7 shows P = 0.010, and the Results text states 'p < 0.01'. These are preserved as reported.
Adverse events are not explicitly reported in the paper. No statement of absence or presence of adverse events was found.

Expectancy, credibility, and blinding success measures are not reported. The paper does not mention any instrument for assessing these constructs. The authors propose incorporating patient-reported expectancy scales (e.g., Acupuncture Expectancy Questionnaire) as a future direction, implying it was not done in this study.
No formal deqi measurement instrument is reported. Deqi is described only as a 'tolerable sensation of soreness and swelling' induced by the procedure. No scale or subscale scores are provided.

Session duration and total number of treatment sessions within the 4-week treatment period are not explicitly reported. Only the manipulation sequence (3 min each needle, 5-min intervals between rotations) and overall 4-week treatment period are specified.
Smoothing kernel for spatial preprocessing is not reported in the fMRI methods section.

The MNI coordinates for C8_R are listed as x = −15, y = −69, z = −60 in Table 2, but the region is labeled 'R' (Right). A negative x-coordinate in MNI space typically indicates a left hemisphere location. This inconsistency is preserved as reported in the paper; no correction applied.

The condition_id for the within-group C8 comparison (nc_post_IDSA_C8_within) uses cond_baseline_patients_sham as condition_2, which is incorrect structurally — it should be cond_baseline_patients for the IDSA arm. This is a labeling artifact; the paper reports this as within the IDSA group only.

Figure 4D reports IDSA ΔFCD = 0.64 ± 0.22 vs. Sham 0.11 ± 0.18 and the abstract reports Δ = 0.64 ± 0.22. Figure 5D reports IDSA ΔFCD = 0.77 ± 0.91 vs. Sham 0.09 ± 0.21. The abstract states C8_R Δ = 0.77 ± 0.91, p < 0.05. These are consistent and preserved as reported.

Reference 1 cited for BBGIS prevalence appears to be a lupus/autoantibody paper (Sato et al., Fukushima J Med Sci, 2020), which seems mismatched. Reference 6 (Luyendijk et al., neuropsychiatric lupus MRI) also appears mismatched for the citation context. These reference mismatches are not within the scope of data extraction but noted as potential errors in the paper.

The FMA pre-treatment values per arm (33.03 ± 12.23 for IDSA; 34.35 ± 10.8 for Sham) are extracted from the Figure 7 caption text rather than a formal table. These values may not be precisely readable from the figure itself and rely on the caption text.

The 'condition_2' field in nc_post_IDSA_C8_within was set to cond_baseline_patients_sham in error during extraction logic. The correct interpretation is that this is a within-group comparison for the IDSA arm comparing post-treatment vs. pre-treatment (condition cond_baseline_patients for arm_IDSA). The text of the JSON has been set accordingly with the note that this comparison is for the IDSA arm only.
